resources.string: Dynamic Island in the style of ColorOS / HyperOS: replaces the One UI Now Bar status bar capsule.
Enable the module for System UI in LSPosed. Changes apply within a few seconds.
Show the app name and time above live notification cards.
Coloured icons in the small island
Keep the real colours of an app icon or a team logo when the island is small. Off shows them in grey.
Drive the music waveform from the real audio output. Off uses a gentle animation instead.
Pop up when a charger is plugged in and when the battery runs low.
Show Silent / Vibrate / Ring when the sound mode changes.
Show headphones and speakers when they connect, with their battery level.
A light tick when the island expands or collapses and a click on its buttons.
Show which app is using the camera or microphone, and open its permissions on tap.
Also announce location use. Off by default: navigation and weather apps use it constantly.
Confirm Do Not Disturb, airplane mode, power saving, flashlight, hotspot and auto-rotate being switched.
While a progress card is on the island, drop the same notification from the shade. Its buttons stay on the card.
Show ongoing notifications with a progress bar (downloads, file copies, app updates) as cards.

Every new notification gets an island card, also the quiet ones that would not pop up as a banner. Ongoing, call and alarm notifications and the app you are in are left out. Experimental: it may not work on every phone or for every app.
Messages and other banner notifications appear as an island card instead of the heads-up banner. Calls and alarms keep the stock banner.
A text with a verification code opens a card with the code and a Copy button.
Put the code on the clipboard as soon as the card appears (replaces what you copied before).
Ongoing calls of voice-chat and VoIP apps get the call card with the running time and an end button.
The status bar and notification shade restart for a moment so the module reloads. Needs root.
Could not restart System UI. Root access was not granted; restart it from the LSPosed manager or reboot.
Words and patterns that tell the island what a notification means (delivery, ride, route, device, codes). Same file format as LiveBridge\'s dictionary.
Delivery, ride, route and device cards
Turn notifications that say \"the rider is almost there\" into a card with the stage they report.

"Default" uses the value of the rule itself, or the module\'s if the rule has none. The first number counts from the moment the notification was posted.

A rule turns a notification into a card with stages. You add its apps and the wording of each stage next.
Pick a name that is not used by another rule.
A rule of the module. Your changes are added on top of it.
A pattern is a regular expression, case does not matter. A notification counts for this stage when the pattern is found in its text. Patterns that could hang the phone are refused.
This pattern is not accepted. Check the brackets, or make it shorter and simpler.
Parts of package names. Untick the ones you added (marked with a pencil) to remove them.

Opening, closing and swapping flow into one another, and a light outline keeps every shape visible on a black screen.

Inspired by @cryyear\'s DynamicIsland (github.com/Spottq) and reimplemented. Rule file format by LiveBridge. Xposed API by rovo89 (Apache-2.0).
Move and resize the island, set the camera hole
The default: the island sits on the camera and grows out of it
In the middle of the status bar, as a plain pill
A quarter of the way in from the left edge
A quarter of the way in from the right edge
Back to the camera hole with no shift
Once it is moved off the camera hole it is drawn as a plain pill. The cards still open in the middle of the screen width.
Look at the real status bar above: the island shows a sample and moves while you change these.

The island grows out of the camera hole and keeps its text away from it. If it sits wrong on your phone, set the hole by hand: a blue ring on the real screen shows where the island thinks the hole is, so line it up with the camera.
Read from the display cutout (the default)
Size and place the hole yourself
A plain pill, text may run across the middle
The island does not shrink again after it has grown, until it hides
The island on the real status bar takes the size as you drag. A higher pill grows its icons with it. With a height change the island keeps its text away from the camera hole as before.
